guides.pageTitle: Havoc Demon Hunter DPS Gear and Best in Slot - 12.1 - World of Warcraft - Icy Veins
guides.author: Wordup

items.name: Zul'jin's Guillotine Technique
items.guideNote: A strong direct damage trinket, but gets stronger when paired with the cantrip weapon, Aman'muso, Warlord's Vengeance. Due to how much damage trinket effects deal through Know Your Enemy, this is so strong that it even remains the strongest pick in AoE situations, and is the strongest trinket available in most Venomous Abyss encounters when enabled.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: Font was already on Havoc's radar due to Know Your Enemy, and due to some additional findings after live release, its performance is much better than expected. The ability to line it up with Initiative to deal incredible damage at key moments makes it an excellent on-use tool regardless of the situation.

items.name: Voracious Heart of Ula'tek
items.guideNote: This is by far the best stat boosting on-use option available in Season 2, despite being on an awkward 1m30s cooldown. This and Font compete for your on-use slot, depending on whether you want to boost your own damage more frequently, or deal front-loaded burst via the trinket itself. Both of these are strong picks.

items.name: Void Execution Mandate
items.guideNote: Try to always use this on a target that will live long enough for you to stack up the Crit buff, else most of its value is lost.

items.name: Sapling of the Dawnroot
items.guideNote: Very single-target focused direct damage trinket, but is an alternative while you hunt for Guillotine Technique. This can, however, have some issues hitting some bosses, so isn't always as strong as sims imply.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Triggers a variety of different stat boosting effects, and different buffs can overlap. While it does have a negative proc in the pool, it's a solid stat trinket. The nerfs leading up to the release of the season though pushed it down a tier.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Can be used on cooldown in single-target, but hold for Metamorphosis in AoE.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: Go to the Jan'alai altar in Zul'Aman to set this to Mastery, or the Akil'zon altar to set it back to Critical Strike, depending on your gearset.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While this is tuned well, staying within the zone of the proc is extremely restrictive, especially for Havoc that moves around frequently. Pair that with both the large arenas in raid encounters and the hectic movement in dungeons, and your mileage may vary in reality when using it.

items.name: Darkmoon Dominion: Hunt
items.guideNote: While these trinket options aren't bad, Embellishments are stronger in Season 2 compared to before. That means the opportunity cost of using them is too high, and they've fallen even further behind than they already were.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: This is our best trinket for Mythic Plus this season, providing a very high uptime secondary stat buff. This is especially useful due to the frequency at which Devourer enters their cooldowns.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Our best on-use available this season, buffing the burst we do at the start of Void Metamorphosis. This should be held and lined up with casts of Void Metamorphosis.

items.name: Wavecaller's Seastone
items.guideNote: Our best passive trinket for Raid encounters. This trinket offers a powerful intellect proc, but does have some ramp up time.

items.name: Fang of Umbral Malignance
items.guideNote: A strong passive damage effect, which triggers often due to the amount of spells Devourer casts. Not as powerful as our best options, but still a great pickup.

items.name: Vile Vial of Volatile Venom
items.guideNote: Our second best on-use trinket. The longer cooldown and slight downside keep it just behind Freightrunner's Flask, but it is still quite powerful. Seek to pair this with Void Metamorphosis.

items.name: Ruby Whelp Shell
items.guideNote: Strong dungeon proc trinket. Seek to train this four times in the crit buff (use it while standing alone) and twice in the haste buff (use it while standing in a group of allies).

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Triggers a variety of different stat boosting effects, and different buffs can overlap. While it does have a negative proc in the pool, it's the best passive stat option available, making it the best pick for any cleave or AoE, and in dungeons.

items.name: Lustrous Golden Plumage
items.guideNote: Certainly not as strong as Voracious Heart, but serves as an on-use alternative from Mythic+. The longer duration also allows it to blanket most of the extended Berserk duration from the new Tier Set.

items.name: Vile Vial of Volatile Venom
items.guideNote: Lines up with Berserk to empower your burst windows, but the negative after-effect kicks in and blankets both the tail end of your cooldowns and the Tier Set payoff, making it slightly weaker than other on-use alternatives.

items.name: Void Execution Mandate
items.guideNote: Try to always use this on a target that will live long enough for you to stack up the Crit buff, else most of its value is lost.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While this is tuned well and Mastery is desirable, staying within the zone of the proc is extremely restrictive, especially in Season 2. Due to both the large arenas in raid encounters and the hectic movement in dungeons, your mileage may vary in reality when using it.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: Go to the Jan'alai altar in Zul'Aman to set this to Mastery.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Hold to line up with Berserk. When using Potion of Recklessness, make sure to pot before using your trinket to avoid setting it to Crit.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage

While it struggles against other options due to it being a channel and a long cooldown, it's unique potential to be useful to deal with key enemies means it might be worth looking at in certain edge cases in Season 2.

items.name: Darkmoon Dominion: Hunt
items.guideNote: While these trinket options aren't bad, Embellishments are stronger in Season 2 compared to before. That means the opportunity cost of using them is too high, and they've fallen even further behind than they already were.

guides.pageTitle: Augmentation Evoker DPS Gear and Best in Slot - 12.1 - World of Warcraft - Icy Veins
guides.author: Saeldur

items.name: Mindpiercer's Sigil
items.guideNote: This is passive trinket that has no stats on it whatsoever, instead having both a damage proc and a main stat proc. This is reasonably well tuned for single-target but is slightly worse than stat trinkets for multi-target encounters.

items.name: Wavecaller's Seastone
items.guideNote: This is passive trinket that provides an intellect buff that rises and falls over an encounter. This trinket is rated highly as it is both highly tuned and scales better on fights with multi-target cleave than damage trinkets do.

items.name: Vexhul's Everflowing Gland
items.guideNote: This is the best on use damage trinket available for this tier. This trinket will get some minor cooldown reduction on fights with adds which will help remain competitive on add fights despite doing pure single-target damage.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: This is a mastery proc trinket that provides a large boost to passive mastery, which is augmentations best stat. This trinket will proc a zone you have to stand in that provides even more mastery. This will always spawn on your head and is quite easy to see but you are not guaranteed to have 100% uptime.

items.name: Fang of Umbral Malignance
items.guideNote: This is a damage proc trinket leaves a stacking DoT on an enemy. This DoT does excellent single-target damage by itself and is the bulk of the contribution in raid as you will not usually get much damage from the explosions.

items.name: Fang of Umbral Malignance
items.guideNote: This is a damage proc trinket leaves a stacking DoT on an enemy. This DoT does reasonable damage by itself but what makes it really powerful in Mythic+ is the extra effect on killing an enemy. These explosions do a lot of damage and heavily reward chainpulling monsters to let the DoT effects cascade onto enemies.

items.name: Mindpiercer's Sigil
items.guideNote: This is passive trinket that has no stats on it whatsoever, instead having both a damage proc and a main stat proc. This is reasonably well tuned for Single Target but is slightly worse than stat trinkets for AoE.

items.name: Wavecaller's Seastone
items.guideNote: This is passive trinket that provides an intellect buff that rises and falls over an encounter. This trinket is rated highly as it is both highly tuned and scales better on fights with multi-target cleave than damage trinkets do.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: This is a high budget stat trinket which provides a strong consistent DPS increase despite Augmentations poor secondary stat scaling. In Mythic+ this is rated higher as Stat Trinkets are stronger relative to raid since the potent damage trinkets usually do not scale.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: This is a mastery proc trinket that provides a large boost to passive mastery, which is augmentations best stat. This trinket will proc a zone you have to stand in that provides even more mastery. This will always spawn on your head and is quite easy to see but you are not guaranteed to have 100% uptime.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: This is a channeled on use trinket that deals an extremely large burst of damage upon being used with a long 4 minute cooldown. This trinket will be useful on bosses that have damage vulnerability phases like Coiled Altar. On other fights this trinket is slightly underperforming compared to other options due to being channeled.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: This is the best on use trinket available this season, very slightly ahead of Vaelgor's Final Stare from Season 1. This trinket is good if you want to improve your burst damage on an encounter, especially for dealing with Adds or damage burns.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: This is a high budget stat trinket which provides a strong consistent DPS increase despite Augmentations poor secondary stat scaling. This trinket is highly rated for AoE damage which makes up a significant portion of this raid.

items.name: Hex Lord's Dooming Idol
items.guideNote: This is an interesting on use trinket that has a ramping negative main stat debuff. When you use the on-use it will remove the debuff and grant you a large on-use buff. This trinket is currently slightly undertuned despite being obtainable at 344 item level. This trinket can be used to great effect on bosses with damage vulnerability phases or adds to shift your damage into those windows.

localizedNames.es: Ídolo de fatalidad de señor aojador

items.name: Vaelgor's Final Stare
items.guideNote: Despite being a trinket from Season 1 this is a highly competitive trinket for Augmentation this tier to get more Burst DPS. At 298 item level this trinket is only outperformed by Myth trinkets. If you do not have this trinket at 298 item level you will not be able to acquire it during this Season and will need to use another trinket.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: This is the second best on use trinket available this season, behind Vaelgor's Final Stare from Season 1. This trinket is good if you want to improve your burst damage on an encounter, especially for dealing with Adds or damage burns.

items.name: Vexhul's Everflowing Gland
items.guideNote: This is a strong single-target damage trinket that is available from the raid. This deals execllent priority and single-target damage throughout a key. Furthermore, this trinket gets additional cooldown reduction when enemies die letting you get more uses over an entire dungeon.

items.name: Hex Lord's Dooming Idol
items.guideNote: This is an interesting on use trinket that has a ramping negative main stat debuff. When you use the on-use it will remove the debuff and grant you a large on-use buff. This trinket lets you shift damage from less relevant parts of a pull, such as the tail end when you are cleaning up a pack, to the start of a pull where DPS have their cds running. Despite this, it is currently slightly undertuned and is only recommended at 344 item level.

localizedNames.es: Ídolo de fatalidad de señor aojador

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: This is a Delve Trinket that can have its stats changed to proc any of the four types. For Augmentation Evoker, we want this trinket to proc Mastery. Use the trinket at the Jan'alai temple to get this stat. Note: Make sure to remove the trinket slot from any macros, as the on-use on this trinket will break your macros.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: This is a channeled on use trinket that deals a large burst of damage upon being used. This trinket is currently undertuned and does not contribute enough damage to outweigh the fact that its a channeled trinket on a very long cooldown, even factoring in that it is available at 344 item level.

guides.pageTitle: Brewmaster Monk Tank Gear and Best in Slot - 12.1 - World of Warcraft - Icy Veins
guides.author: Sinzhu

items.name: Voracious Heart of Ula'tek
items.guideNote: With static Critical Strike, on-demand Agility every 90 seconds, bonus Physical damage that interacts with your tier set and the Shado-Pan talents, and an increased item level on Mythic, this trinket has absolutely everything you would want as a Brewmaster. Seek it out, even on Heroic.

items.name: Zul'jin's Guillotine Technique
items.guideNote: While it may be part of a set effect with Aman'muso, Warlord's Vengeance, this trinket's baseline 3ppm effect is strong enough on its own to be a valuable pickup. The extra item level on Mythic certainly helps, too, as does its Physical damage being enhanced by both your tier set and the Shado-Pan Hero Talents.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: Its 4-minute cooldown is hefty, and you are unable to dodge attacks during its channel, but the damage output of this trinket is particularly exceptional in single-target. It is your strongest option for burst damage, especially at its Mythic item level of 344.

items.name: Tumor of the Swarm
items.guideNote: Although this is a tank trinket, its damage is surprisingly potent while also providing a helpful stream of healing at a rate of 3ppm. In spite of splitting its damage among enemies, the total amount dealt per proc also increases, making it an incredibly passive, "hybrid" option for AoE.

items.name: Lustrous Golden Plumage
items.guideNote: Perhaps your most useful on-use trinket if not able to receive "elevated" 344 options, this item provides a large burst of Versatility when you need for 20 seconds every 2 minutes. This lines up nicely with Invoke Niuzao, the Black Ox, but only for Master of Harmony Brewmasters.

items.name: Tiny Electromental in a Jar
items.guideNote: Still just as strong as it was in Battle for Azeroth, this trinket builds roughly 20 charges per minute and unleashes Nature damage with every 12 accumulated. By also including a chaining effect, it remains potent across a variety of target counts while being an option that is easy enough to obtain from Mythic+.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: This trinket is incredible for Shado-Pan players in particular, as its 90-second on-use cooldown for bonus Critical Strike lines up nicely with the reduced cooldown on Invoke Niuzao, the Black Ox available to this set of Hero Talents. However, Master of Harmony users will still find it quite potent.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Why? This trinket can trigger one of seven different effects at a rate of 3ppm:

items.name: Vashnik's Sanguine Rancor
items.guideNote: By offering benefits to its damage (triggering roughly once per minute) against only a single target and also against multiple, this trinket is a convenient universal and passive option for damage.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While this trinket does provide a useful amount of Mastery, remember that you must be able to stand in its light beam to gain its full benefit; this may not always be feasible in the middle of combat.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: (Crit)

items.name: Keeper's Seething Core
items.guideNote: You may be wondering how a trinket with Haste can be placed so highly. This is largely because of the stat's potential to scale with your AoE damage in particular, while also triggering more applications of your 4-set bonus by helping to reduce the cooldown of Keg Smash. And, with a generous proc rate of 6 per minute, you will frequently trigger the 20% bonus effect as well!

items.name: Ruby Whelp Shell
items.guideNote: Why? Much of this trinket's value depends on how you take advantage of the ability to "train" the whelp it spawns over the course of a week. By doing so, you can have it properly prioritize one of the following effects approximately once per minute:

items.name: Darkmoon Dominion: Void
items.guideNote: While this trinket can only be obtained at a static item level and will quickly be outscaled by "worse" alternatives, it is enhanced if paired with a crafted weapon featuring a matching embellishment ( Darkmoon Sigil: Void).

localizedNames.es: Dominio de la Luna Negra: Vacío

items.name: Magister's Alchemist Stone
items.guideNote: This trinket is surprisingly strong for having an effect similar to alchemist stones of every prior expansion. However, in Midnight this item counts as an embellished piece of gear, making it difficult to justify.

guides.pageTitle: Enhancement Shaman DPS Gear and Best in Slot - 12.1 - World of Warcraft - Icy Veins
guides.author: Wordup

items.name: Voracious Heart of Ula'tek
items.guideNote: This is by far the best on-use option available in Season 2, despite being on an awkward 1m30s cooldown. No other option comes close in power, so this is one of your big chase items. Always hold it to line up with your Ascendance or Surging Totem window.

items.name: Zul'jin's Guillotine Technique
items.guideNote: A stock-standard direct damage trinket, but gets stronger when paired with the cantrip weapon, Aman'muso, Warlord's Vengeance. This has less uses in AoE content, but for single-target and especially cleave within the raid it's the strongest passive option available.

items.name: Vile Vial of Volatile Venom
items.guideNote: Definitely not as strong as Voracious Heart, but a good alternative if you're in need of an on-use. When using it and Potion of Recklessness together, make sure to pot before activating this to avoid increasing the wrong stat.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Triggers a variety of different stat boosting effects, and different buffs can overlap. While it does have a negative proc in the pool, it's the best passive stat option available, making it a good pick for AoE heavy encounters and dungeons.

items.name: Void Execution Mandate
items.guideNote: Try to always use this on a target that will live long enough for you to stack up the Crit buff, else most of its value is lost.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Hold to line up with Ascendance / Surging Totem depending on build. When using Potion of Recklessness, make sure to pot before using your trinket to avoid setting it to Crit.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While this is tuned well and Mastery is desirable, staying within the zone of the proc is extremely restrictive, especially in Season 2. Due to both the large arenas in raid encounters and the hectic movement in dungeons, your mileage may vary in reality when using it.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: Go to the Jan'alai altar in Zul'Aman to set this to Mastery.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: This deals an extremely large amount of burst damage to your primary target when used, alongside some bonus AoE. While it struggles against other options due to it being a channel and a long cooldown, it's unique potential to be useful to deal with key enemies means it might be worth looking at in certain edge cases in Season 2.

items.name: Tattered Amani War Banner
items.guideNote: Hold to line up with Ascendance / Surging Totem depending on build.

items.name: Darkmoon Dominion: Hunt
items.guideNote: While these trinket options aren't bad, Embellishments are stronger in Season 2 compared to before. That means the opportunity cost of using them is too high, and they've fallen even further behind than they already were.

localizedNames.es: Recipiente ritual de volutador de almas

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: A strong passive trinket which occasionally will cause you to lose stats rather than gain them, but overall its effect is mostly positive and powerful with great uptime.

items.name: Wavecaller's Seastone
items.guideNote: This is a strong passive trinket, which grants a lot of Intellect in cycles and is very powerful if you can time your healing cooldowns with the periods where it is at its maximum stacks.

items.name: Hex Lord's Dooming Idol
items.guideNote: This trinket actively stacks an Intellect debuff until you use it, at which point you get a massive Intellect boost, which is great to really empower your burst healing potential, at the cost of lowered power in between burst windows.

localizedNames.es: Ídolo de fatalidad de señor aojador

items.name: Ruby Whelp Shell
items.guideNote: This trinket can be trained by using it on yourself with it when alone and out of combat to provide you with random procs of extra critical strike, in which case it is a strong stat stick, similar to Wavecaller's Seastone.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Simple trinket with critical strike on use, which you should delay slightly to align with 2-minute Ascendance or use on cooldown to perfectly align with the 3-minute version.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: A very strong delve trinket which you can configure to provide a reliable crit proc by using it on the Zul'Aman zone at the 52.15 80.74 map coordinates.

items.name: Glorious Crusader's Keepsake
items.guideNote: A fantastic trinket that cannot be obtained as Myth track, but is well worth using early on, even if you are the only player with it in the group.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While it is especially good if you can stand in the Mastery beam it occasionally provides, most of its benefit comes passively, allowing you to use it for its stats alone.

items.name: Vile Vial of Volatile Venom
items.guideNote: Using this grants you a powerful random stat buff for 15 seconds on a 2-minute cooldown, which is ideal to pair with 2-minute Ascendance. Unfortunately it will also cause you to lose a lower amount of stats for 15 seconds after its effect expires, which makes it more of a burst healing trinket.

items.name: Unstable Felheart Crystal
items.guideNote: A powerful Mythic+ trinket for lifesaving on-use purposes.

items.name: Seed of Radiant Hope
items.guideNote: A powerful Mythic+ trinket for lifesaving on-use purposes, although its effect can take a while to activate since it depends on the person you used it on dropping low health.

items.name: Mycolic Medicine
items.guideNote: Fairly decent and provides most of its benefit passively like Lightspire Core, but is slightly less powerful due to having a flat heal effect rather than Mastery potential multiplier for your healing.

items.name: Stormbound Emblem of Dazar
items.guideNote: This trinket provides an on-use burst of Haste every 2 minutes, making it a perfect pair to 2-minute Ascendance.

localizedNames.es: Emblema de Dazar vinculado a la tormenta
